disclosure: Tech Watch entries are short summaries of publicly available video content, drafted from automatic captions and reviewed before publication. They describe what the linked source videos discuss; they are not verified factual claims and are not analytical assessments. See Analyst Notes for sourced, confidence-labeled analysis.

items.blurb: A DARPA series on efforts to put AI development on a firmer theoretical footing. Segments cover research approaches from Princeton and Harvard teams, hyperparameter tuning, model-agnostic scaling principles, treating deep neural networks as physical systems, faster training, AI-driven benchmarking of language models, and open research questions.
items.headline: DARPA AIQ: building a theory of how AI models scale and train

items.blurb: Discusses the reported loss of components removed from an Australian F-35A and sent to the United States for inspection, which later surfaced in Hong Kong, reportedly including a weapons bay door. Covers the shipping and repair chain, the F-35 program's acknowledgment of the loss, and the potential intelligence value of the parts. A companion video covers synthetic gemstones used in the F-35's targeting systems.
items.headline: F-35 parts removed from an Australian jet surface in Hong Kong

videos.title: The F-35 Parts That Somehow Ended Up in Hong Kong

items.blurb: DARPA's own overview of the Quantum Benchmarking Initiative, which asks whether any approach can reach utility-scale quantum computing by 2033. Covers the program's staged evaluation, from concept review through independent government verification of competing hardware approaches, and frames the effort as a race to separate credible designs from roadmaps.
items.headline: DARPA Quantum Benchmarking Initiative: verifying a path to useful quantum computing
